Hypersensitivity reactions, including symptoms such as difficulty breathing (dyspnea), swelling of the face, mouth, or throat (angioedema), skin rash, and itching (pruritus), have been reported with the use of fidaxomicin. If such a reaction occurs, the medication should be discontinued immediately, and appropriate medical treatment should be initiated. 2. Fidaxomicin should only be used for infections that are either proven or strongly suspected to be caused by Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This is to minimize the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. Due to its minimal systemic absorption, fidaxomicin is not effective for treating other types of infections. 3. Acute hypersensitivity reactions have been observed in some patients, and a history of allergy to other macrolide antibiotics (e.g., azithromycin, clarithromycin) has been reported in certain cases. Patients with such a history should be monitored closely. 4. The use of fidaxomicin in the absence of a confirmed or strongly suspected C. difficile infection is unlikely to benefit the patient and may increase the risk of drug-resistant bacterial development. 5. There is limited data on the use of fidaxomicin in pregnant women, and the available information is insufficient to determine any drug-associated risks for major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes. 6. It is unknown whether fidaxomicin or its primary metabolite, OP-1118, is present in human breast milk, or what effects it may have on a breastfed infant or milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for fidaxomicin and any potential adverse effects on the infant from the medication or the underlying maternal condition. 7. Fidaxomicin is metabolized by hydrolysis at the isobutyryl ester to form its active metabolite, OP-1118. The drug has a half-life of approximately 9 hours and is primarily excreted in the feces (92%). 8. When preparing the oral suspension, the glass bottle should be shaken to ensure the granules move freely and are not caked. Add 130 mL of purified water to the bottle, cap it tightly, and shake vigorously in a horizontal position for at least 2 minutes. Verify that a homogeneous suspension has been achieved; if not, repeat the shaking process. Once a uniform suspension is visually confirmed, shake for an additional 30 seconds. Allow the bottle to stand for 1 minute and verify that the suspension remains homogeneous. If not, repeat the shaking instructions. The reconstituted suspension should appear white to yellowish-white in color. 9. Write the discard date (12 days from the date of preparation) on the bottle. The medication may be taken with or without food. 10. Fidaxomicin is used to treat severe intestinal infections caused by C. difficile, which can occur after antibiotic use. Symptoms of this condition include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain or cramping, and blood or mucus in the stool. Fidaxomicin is a macrolide antibiotic that works locally in the intestines and is not absorbed into the bloodstream. It is not effective for other types of infections, including viral infections like the common cold or flu. 11. Take fidaxomicin as directed by your doctor, usually twice daily (every 12 hours). If using the liquid form, remove the bottle from the refrigerator 15 minutes before use and shake well before each dose. Measure the dose carefully using a special measuring device or spoon. For optimal effectiveness, take the medication at evenly spaced intervals and complete the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. 12. Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain. Serious allergic reactions are rare but can occur. If you experience severe symptoms such as difficulty breathing or swelling, seek immediate medical attention. 13. Before taking fidaxomicin, inform your doctor if you are allergic to it, other macrolide antibiotics, or any inactive ingredients in the product. This medication may interfere with live bacterial vaccines (e.g., typhoid vaccine), reducing their effectiveness. 14. During pregnancy, fidaxomicin should only be used if clearly needed. It is unknown whether the drug passes into breast milk. 15. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of fidaxomicin or increase the risk of side effects. Keep a list of all medications and supplements you are taking and share it with your healthcare provider. 16. In case of overdose, seek emergency medical attention or contact a poison control center immediately. In the U.S., call 1-800-222-1222. 17. Store fidaxomicin tablets at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Liquid medication should be stored in the refrigerator in its original bottle and discarded after 12 days. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly. 18. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about fidaxomicin and your specific health needs.
